description: Alipur 13FT Resilience: brother-sister team from Alipur, Muzaffargarh, South Punjab. In 2025, Basti Mazaari flood hit 13FT, power lost for weeks. Our idea: flood-resilient, cyber-secure solar microgrids for rural schools using NASA Earth data. Concept by Ahmad Raza, BS Cyber Security, Aspire Leaders grad. Training in Saraiki/Urdu.
summary:
Project Alipur 13FT Resilience - Summary

We developed a decentralized, flood-resilient solar micro-grid for Basti Mazaari, Alipur, District Muzaffargarh, where the Indus and Chenab rivers meet.

In 2025, Eastern Punjab faced its worst flood in history. According to UN-OCHA, 3.9 million people were affected and 3,952 villages were inundated. In Muzaffargarh, 40,000 people waited on rooftops for rescue. NASA Earth Observatory (11 Sept 2025) confirmed from space that rainfall was 21% above normal in Pakistan and 36% in Punjab, and all four rivers flooded together.

Our problem: when the centralized grid floods, it shuts down. Hospitals, water pumps and shelters go dark.

Our solution: solar panels installed 13FT above the 2025 flood level, with automated battery storage. The system works in 4 steps - DETECT, DETACH, DELIVER, DEFEND. It detects flood risk from NASA data, detaches from the main grid into island mode, delivers power to schools and shelters, and defends IoT sensors with cybersecurity.

This turns our flood-affected community from victims into a model of climate resilience.
details:
What does it do? Hello, my name is Ahmad Raza from Alipur, District Muzaffargarh. My district sits where the Indus and Chenab rivers meet. According to UN-OCHA Flash Update #6, in 2025 Eastern Punjab endured its worst flood in history, with almost 3.9 million people affected and 3,952 villages inundated, with Muzaffargarh and Multan severely affected. Flash Update #8 reported that 40,000 people in my district Muzaffargarh were in urgent need, waiting on rooftops and trees for rescue. And the UN's final strategy report declared Muzaffargarh a High Priority District for six months of recovery. What NASA Data Shows: NASA Earth Observatory confirmed this disaster from space. In its report "Monsoon Rains Flood Pakistan" (11 Sept 2025), NASA showed with MODIS Terra satellite image of 29 Aug 2025 and VIIRS data from NOAA-20 satellite, how the Indus, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej rivers all flooded at the same time. NASA reported that monsoon rainfall was 21% above normal in Pakistan and 36% above normal in Punjab, and that nearly 4 million people were affected in Eastern Punjab and close to 2 million were evacuated. NASA also reported that an estimated 75% of Pakistan's farmland was harmed. This NASA satellite proof matches exactly what we saw on the ground in Alipur - water everywhere, no power, no way out. I saw the real problem: when the centralized power grid floods, it shuts down. Hospitals, water pumps, and shelters go into total darkness. My solution is: Decentralized, flood-resilient solar micro-grids with automated battery storage. These small local grids can detach from the main grid and keep running during floods. We call it Alipur 13FT Resilience - solar panels installed 13FT above the 2025 flood level in Basti Mazaari, Alipur. How does it work? 1. DETECT: We use NASA Earth data - rainfall, soil moisture, and river level from NASA Earthdata and NASA Earth Observatory - and UN-OCHA flood reports to detect flood trends in the Indus, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej rivers. When flood risk is high, the system sends an alert to local leaders. 2. DETACH: Before the flood hits, our local microgrid automatically disconnects from the main centralized grid. This is called island mode. So even if the main grid shuts down, our school keeps running. 3. DELIVER: Solar panels at 13FT height keep generating power above the water. Automated battery storage stores power for night and cloudy days. It powers lights, fans, water pumps, internet, computers and mobile charging in schools and shelters. 4. DEFEND: As a Cybersecurity student, my unique angle is security. These smart grids use IoT sensors. If they are hacked during an emergency, the humanitarian cost is fatal. I want to build the cybersecurity framework to protect this clean energy - encrypted sensors, secure access, and safe shutdown. Our Plan for Basti Mazaari: We will start with one pilot in Basti Mazaari, Alipur. First, we will install one solar micro-grid on the school roof at 13FT height with battery storage. Second, the system is fully automatic - teachers and students will not need to operate it, a local solar technician will handle maintenance. Third, we will connect the school as a community shelter - so during flood, families can charge phones, get clean water from solar pump, and get light at night. If this one pilot succeeds, the same low-cost model can be copied in every flood-affected village of Muzaffargarh without waiting for the big grid to come back. Who will benefit? What is the impact?

Direct benefit: Students and teachers in rural schools in Basti Mazaari, Alipur, who will not lose classes during floods. Wider benefit: Hospitals, water pumps, and shelters in Muzaffargarh will have backup power. Women and children are priority, because they suffer most in displacement camps. Long-term benefit: This project will turn my flood-affected community from victims into a model of climate resilience. The model can be replicated in all South Punjab - Jhang, Khanewal, Bahawalpur, Multan. What tools and data did you use? Data: NASA Earth Observatory - Monsoon Rains Flood Pakistan (11 Sept 2025, MODIS Terra 29 Aug 2025, VIIRS NOAA-20), NASA Earthdata for rainfall (21% above normal, 36% in Punjab) and river level, UN-OCHA Flash Update #6 and #8, UN-OCHA Support Plan for Relief & Early Recovery 2025 (Muzaffargarh - High Priority District). Tools: NASA Earth Observatory, NASA Earthdata, UN-OCHA ReliefWeb, Meta AI for writing and image support, Canva for slides, Google Drive for PDF sharing. Low-cost, local design, no heavy coding needed for prototype. Why is it creative and different? Most solar projects only talk about energy. We combined three things in one local solution: 1) Flood Data + 2) Solar Energy + 3) Cyber-Security. Our idea is not from a book, it is from lived experience - seeing 40,000 people on rooftops in my own district, waiting for rescue in darkness. We don't just want to rebuild, we want to build resilient. This project will turn my flood-affected community from victims into a model of climate resilience. Thank you. Team Alipur 13FT Resilience, Ahmad Raza & Rida Zahra.
